meta.title: Unique Pokémon
meta.description: The hub's Unique Lab: five rotating slots of 'unique' Pokémon — species from the game's base-stage, non-legendary roster (rolled under the default Pokédex, not your active one) reborn with bonus moves, special abilities or swapped types, rolled across four rarities. A 'Unique Pokémon detected nearby' alert tells you one is in the wild, and catching one converts it (keeping its IVs and shiny) and consumes the slot. The system is the same in both versions; EX enriches it with a bigger bonus-ability pool (44 to 63 abilities) and a different set of default exotic species.

prose.heading: Pokémon no one else can get
prose.text: A unique Pokémon is a normal base-stage species — from the game's full roster with legendaries excluded, and rolled with the Pokédex temporarily forced to its default variant, so which dex you have active never changes the pool — reborn with extras: bonus moves drawn from a curated pool, a special ability, or even a swapped type. They are 'dynamic' — the same species can produce a different unique mon every time it is rolled — and they are tracked through five lab slots in your save, which are re-rolled when a run begins and when it ends. When one is out in the wild on your current route, a 'Unique Pokémon — Detected nearby!' alert pops up, and if you catch it, it joins your party as that special set with a 'Unique Pokémon' ceremony.

prose.heading: How the lab works
prose.text: The Unique Lab hub upgrade unlocks the first three of five slots; two further slot upgrades add the rest. Each slot rolls a rarity — Common, Rare, Epic or Exotic — and a species (a flat-random pick from the roster, never duplicating a species already active in another slot), then counts down in in-game minutes (slot one expires fastest, the fifth slowest). When the clock hits zero the slot goes empty and is re-rolled at the next run boundary — a run's start or end — so the lab is always churning. Higher rarities need higher lab upgrades: without the Epic upgrade, an Epic roll downgrades to Rare, and so on.

prose.heading: Hunting a unique
prose.text: The detection alert fires on routes only: step into a route whose wild table includes one of your active unique species and a 'Unique Pokémon — Detected nearby!' alert pops up — it only warns that a match is possible, it never guarantees the encounter. Wild dens stay quiet for the alert but can still roll a unique (the same 50/50 conversion); legendary rooms never do — the game's hook there is a commented-out TODO. There's a 50/50 chance a matching wild battle on a route or in a den is actually the unique form — it fights with its bonus moves and ability, gets the slow 'important battle' intro, and keeps whatever shiny state it had. Catch it and the conversion is respectful of your luck: IVs, shiny, gender and nickname all carry over, the mon is healed to at least half health and cured of status, your Strength Charms/Curses adjust its IVs, and the slot it came from is consumed.

records.name: Unique Pokémon (system)
records.description: Five save slots (DYNAMIC_UNIQUE_MON_COUNT 5) hold 'dynamic' custom mons: species rolled from the game's base-stage, non-legendary roster — the roll forces the Pokédex to its default variant, so your active dex never changes the pool — each with a rarity and a countdown. The slots are refreshed when a run begins and when it ends (the same refresh re-rolls any slot whose countdown has expired), and any species on your current route's wild table triggers the detection alert. The system is identical in both versions; the pools of bonus abilities and default exotic species differ.
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L814 / @origin/expansion L816 (DYNAMIC_UNIQUE_MON_COUNT 5); src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1222-1324 (slot fill/refresh: dex variant forced to default L1231-1232, roster query L1234-1237, variant restored L1265) / @origin/expansion L1228-1330 (L1237-1238, L1240-1243, L1271); src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L4649 (refresh at run start), L4895 (refresh at run end), L3482-3484 (countdown ticks every in-game minute) / @origin/expansion L4640, L4886, L3473-3475

records.name: Lab slots and upgrades
records.description: The base Unique Lab hub upgrade unlocks slots 1–3; two further upgrades ('Lab Slots') unlock slot 4 and slot 5. Each active slot counts down in in-game minutes, starting faster for lower slots: slot 1 starts at 60 minutes and each higher slot starts 30 minutes later (60, 90, 120, 150, 180 for slots 1–5), so slots expire on a rolling basis and are re-rolled at the next run boundary (a run's start or end). Expired slots are compacted so the active unique mons always sit in the first slots.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1150-1166 (slot unlock: base lab → slots 0–2, slot 3 → SLOTS0 upgrade, slot 4 → SLOTS1 upgrade), L1299 (countdown 60 + 30 × slot), L1268-1286 (expired/empty slots compacted) / @origin/expansion L1156-1172, L1305, L1274-1292

records.name: Rarity roll
records.description: Each slot roll is Random() % 7: one in seven is Exotic, two in seven Epic, two in seven Rare and two in seven Common. The result is then downgraded through any rarities your lab upgrades don't yet support (Exotic→Epic without the Exotic upgrade, Epic→Rare, Rare→Common), so a brand-new lab only ever rolls Commons until it is upgraded.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1107-1148 / @origin/expansion L1113-1154 (RandomRarity: 1/7 Exotic, 2/7 Epic, 2/7 Rare, 2/7 Common, then downgrade chain by lab rarity upgrades)

records.name: Common
records.description: The everyday rarity: two bonus moves drawn from the curated pool. With the Unique Typings lab upgrade, a Common roll can instead be a type-swapped mon (a single random type, no bonus moves).
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1008-1012 (Common: move1+move2, original format), L1032-1034 (Common: type only, mon-type format) / @origin/expansion L1014-1018, L1038-1040; include/rogue_gifts.h @vanilla L5-11 (rarity comments) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Rare
records.description: One bonus move plus a special ability from the curated pool. With the Unique Typings lab upgrade, a Rare roll can instead be a type-swapped mon with two bonus moves.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1014-1017 (Rare: move1 + ability, original format), L1036-1039 (Rare: type + 2 moves, mon-type format) / @origin/expansion L1020-1023, L1042-1045

records.name: Epic
records.description: Three bonus moves plus a special ability — the strongest 'rolled' rarity. With the Unique Typings lab upgrade, an Epic roll can instead be a type-swapped mon with two bonus moves and a special ability.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1019-1024 (Epic: move1+move2+move3 + ability, original format), L1041-1045 (Epic: type + 2 moves + ability, mon-type format) / @origin/expansion L1025-1030, L1047-1051

records.name: Exotic
records.description: The jackpot roll (1 in 7): instead of a random bonus set, the slot holds a bespoke 'Exotic' mon from the static custom pool — the special mons tied to quests and default spawns. An Exotic slot picks an unused unlocked Exotic mon, and if every one is already in play it falls back to an Epic roll. Requires the Exotic lab upgrade or it downgrades.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1107-1148 (1/7 Exotic + the downgrade chain), L1301-1317 (Exotic slot: unused unlocked exotic mon, Epic fallback) / @origin/expansion L1113-1154, L1307-1323; src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L1181-1220 / @origin/expansion L1187-1226 (SelectUnusedUnlockedExoticMon: default-spawn custom mons + unlocked quest mons)

records.name: Bonus move pool
records.description: Bonus moves are drawn from a curated in-game list (the sDynamicCustomMonMoves table), excluding anything the species already learns by level-up or from tutors — so a unique mon's bonus set is always genuinely new to it. The available pool grows in EX, which adds newer-generation moves to the table.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L983-995 / @origin/expansion L989-1001 (query: include curated move pool, exclude the species' level-up and tutor moves); src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla (sDynamicCustomMonMoves table, extended in EX) / @origin/expansion (larger table)

records.name: Special ability pool
records.description: A unique mon's special ability is drawn from a curated pool of strong abilities. This is one of the version differences in the feature: Vanilla's pool is a modest 44-ability Gen 1–3 list (Drizzle, Static, Water Absorb, Battle Armor and their peers), while EX's pool grows to 63 abilities, adding the Surge abilities, Multiscale, Protean, Magic Bounce, Regenerator and friends.

differences.vanilla: Small Gen 1–3 ability pool of 44 entries (Drizzle, Speed Boost, Battle Armor, Limber, Sand Veil, Static, Volt Absorb, Water Absorb, and similar).
differences.ex: Large Gen 1–9 pool of 63 abilities including Electric/Psychic/Misty/Grassy Surge, Prankster, Multiscale, Protean, Magic Bounce, Regenerator, Mold Breaker and more.

records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L118-161 (Vanilla pool: 44 Gen 1–3 abilities in the #else branch) / @origin/expansion L54-116 (expanded 63-ability Gen 1–9 pool behind #ifdef ROGUE_EXPANSION)

records.name: Unique Typings (lab upgrade)
records.description: A lab upgrade that changes the format of rolled unique mons: instead of bonus moves and abilities, a mon can get a swapped type — its primary type is replaced with a random one that fits its typing rules. Available from Common (type only) up to Epic (type + two moves + ability). Without the upgrade, all rolls use the standard bonus-move format.
records.source: src/rogue_gifts.c @vanilla L975-981 (mon-type format locked behind HUB_UPGRADE_LAB_UNIQUE_TYPINGS), L1028-1046 (per-rarity mon-type payloads) / @origin/expansion L981-987, L1034-1052; data/hub.json (the lab upgrade's cost and requirements are documented on the Hub page)

records.name: 'Unique Pokémon — Detected nearby!'
records.description: When you enter a route, the game checks the route's wild encounter table against your active unique slots, and any match fires the 'Unique Pokémon — Detected nearby!' alert — it warns that a match is possible, it never guarantees the encounter. The check is route-only: wild dens and legendary rooms never fire the alert, though a den can still roll a unique (the same 50% conversion, silently); legendary rooms never do, since the game's hook there is a commented-out TODO. Shiny and unique wilds also get the slow 'important battle' intro when you engage them.
records.source: src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L5843-5883 / @origin/expansion L5834-5874 (route room-entry case: wild encounter table vs active unique slots, popup pushed on match — the den and legendary room cases have no such check); src/rogue_popup.c @vanilla L298-299 (alert text), L1793-1801 (popup push) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L543-547 / @origin/expansion L543-547 (shiny/unique wilds are 'important battles')

records.name: The 50% unique wild
records.description: Not every matching wild is the unique one: on routes and in wild dens, when a wild mon's species matches an active unique slot, there's a 50% chance the battle uses the custom set (bonus moves/ability/type) — otherwise it fights as a normal wild. The conversion happens in place and deliberately preserves the mon's shiny state. The function's gate also admits legendary rooms, but the game's call there is a commented-out TODO — so a legendary-room wild is never unique.
records.source: src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L8469-8506 (TryApplyCustomMon: Room gate, 1-in-2 chance at L8489, shiny preserved) / @origin/expansion L8460-8497 (chance at L8480); src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L8630-8662 (wild-den call L8661) and L8687-8690 (routes, the default branch L8689) — the legendary room's call L8669 is commented out / @origin/expansion L8621-8653 (call L8652), L8678-8681 (call L8680), commented call L8660

records.name: Catching a unique
records.description: When you catch the unique form, the mon is converted to its custom set while keeping its IVs, shiny, gender and nickname. It's then healed to at least half of its max HP, cured of any status, and its IVs are adjusted by your net Strength Charms/Curses. The lab slot that produced it is consumed — that unique is now yours, not a rolling slot.
records.source: src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L1229-1280 / @origin/expansion L1229-1280 (Rogue_ModifyCaughtMon: convert, remove the dynamic mon, heal to 1/2, cure status, IV charm/curse)

records.name: The static custom pool
records.description: Behind the dynamic rolls sits a static pool of 37 bespoke custom mons: Kurt (a shiny Stantler), Pikin (a special Mareep), Wahey's Electrode and Wobbuffet, and a long list of 'Exotic' mons (Farfetch'd, Castform, Pikachu, Lugia and more) used as Exotic-slot fills and quest rewards. Several entries are version-gated at build time, so the default-spawn exotic species differ: Vanilla uses Chimecho, Aron, Misdreavus, Hoothoot, Azurill and Ekans, while EX uses Tympole, Burmy, Carbink, Wattrel, Shinx, Venipede and Trapinch.

differences.vanilla: Default-spawn exotic species are the Gen 1–3 set (Chimecho, Aron, Misdreavus, Hoothoot, Azurill, Ekans) and Pikin carries a Gen 3 move set.
differences.ex: Default-spawn exotic species are the newer set (Tympole, Burmy, Carbink, Wattrel, Shinx, Venipede, Trapinch), Pikin carries an EX move set with Fluffy/Teravolt, and Pikin can Mega Evolve (the Mega form is excluded from custom-mon lookups because it has its own ability).

records.source: src/data/rogue/custom_mons.json @vanilla (37 static custom mons, '#if' build-time version gates) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_gifts.c @origin/expansion L577-581 (EX-only PIKIN_MEGA exception in the custom-mon lookup — the file's only divergence, absent from @vanilla)
